fact: Agence Ecofin states that the Central African Republic has two terrestrial fibre links with its neighbours today, the routes through Cameroon and Congo-Brazzaville, carried by the roughly 935 km Central African Backbone network.
The article says CAR authorities estimated in May 2026 that connecting the country to submarine cables through the terrestrial networks of coastal countries had markedly improved available speeds.

On 8 October 2026 in Moscow the CAR and DRC digital ministers agreed on the need to carry out the CAR-DRC fibre interconnection, which would reach the Moanda submarine cable landing; no timetable or financing agreement was announced.
The article says CAR drew closer to South Sudan around a connectivity project announced in May 2026; its route, timetable and technical terms have not been detailed.

The African Development Bank release says CAR inaugurated its national fibre backbone on 6 February 2023: 935 km of terrestrial and under-river fibre installed and operating, interconnecting CAR with Cameroon (via Gamboula) and Congo (via Bomassa).

Africa50 and Bayobab (MTN) partnered in May 2023 to co-develop Project East2West, a USD 320-325 million terrestrial fibre network linking landlocked countries to coastal cables, and the Central African Republic is among the countries the record names.

The African Development Bank says the Central African Backbone project closed in September 2023 having installed a 900 km national fibre backbone, with terrestrial optical interconnections to Cameroon and Congo, funded by EUR 17m from the EU, EUR 13m from the African Development Fund and EUR 4m from the Bank's Transition Support Facility.

The Central African Republic's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications states that the government received AfDB and European Union grants to cover the cost of the Central African Backbone (CAB) project, RCA component, whose aim is terrestrial fibre-optic interconnections between Central African countries; the notice gives no date for the grants, so the notice's published date of 2018-07-17 is used.

fact: Tech Africa News, citing ITU analysis, says the six CEMAC countries are developing the Central African Backbone to interconnect their national fibre networks, backed by about $273 million from member states and partners, and treats it as the framework for the Central African Republic; it gives no event date, so the article's published date of 2026-08-27 is used.

A PIDA project prospectus sponsored by the ECCAS Secretariat lists the Central African Republic among 11 countries in a USD 9m project to set up six new data centres (one in the CAR) and reinforce five others, to regionalize intra-ECCAS data exchange, showing 25% progress but project stage 'Project Definition'; the page carries no date of its own, so the published date is used.
